research_concepts: placebo validation of a lineup-based design
methodological_questions: Does substituting the offensive five detectably change shot mix (rim, midrange, 3PA, drive, post-up) relative to a placebo or null comparison?
Is the question a falsifiable test or a presupposed conclusion, given it is phrased as already showing that the design can detect personnel effects?
Can within-team, within-game lineup changes separate personnel effects from matchup, fatigue, score-state and game-script confounding?
Is the 2022-23 to 2024-25 play-by-play sample powered to detect a pre-specified minimum shot-mix shift for offensive-five changes?

historical_evidence.finding: Studied opponent lineup adaptation (shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor), not the offensive five. Hypothesis: offenses attack the rim more when no opposing big is present. Results: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25, t=+3.3); POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18, t=+2.4); 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31, t=-5.8); rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4); PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007, t=+1.1). Sample N=1.07M possessions. Recorded verdict: WEAK/SMALL, will not carry a paper. Uses the same play-by-play-reconstructed-lineup dataset.

Final checks family covering a Design 5 placebo, split-half (odd/even game) reliability of team-season H2-H1 change, and an early-vs-rest possession dip. Recorded verdict: inconclusive. Result NOT_RECORDED, sample and power NOT_RECORDED, and 'No log saved.' This is the only retrieved record that names a Design 5 placebo, but it has no reported outcome.

Decision-value test of kernel argmax vs NBA baseline. The v1 version showed an apparent edge of -4.51 pts/100 that was attributed to leakage; after the v2 fix the edge was -1.48 pts/100, with the baseline winning on 23,922 possessions in both versions. Recommendations were CUT about 88% of the time versus an actual rate of 6.8%. Not a direct test of offensive-five effects, but it documents leakage and construction artifacts in this project's play-by-play pipeline.

Opener recommendations vs personnel feasibility. Every rank-1 opener was CUT-centred and infeasible for the top-8 rotation (CUT target 14-18% vs ceiling 2-6%). The optimizer ignored personnel. Not a test of shot-mix response to lineup change, but it shows that personnel feasibility was not modelled in earlier work on this data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Kernel model A decision-value claim using play-type recommendations versus a league-adjusted baseline
failed_approaches.why: Leakage in v1 (-4.51 pts/100 apparent edge); after the v2 fix the baseline still won, and the record classifies the result as C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw). Auto-limited by leakage, with drift/non-stationarity and lookahead risks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Rank-1 opener recommendations tested against personnel feasibility
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the optimizer ignored personnel, and the CUT target exceeded the stretch ceiling by 3-10x in every team-game. Auto-limited by small sample, with base-rate, drift and sample-size risks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Final checks including the Design 5 placebo and split-half reliability of the defensive H2 adjustment trait
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear (mechanism unclear from the records); the log was not saved, so no result, sample or power is available. The placebo therefore has no evidence behind it.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a shot-mix response to a lineup condition (opposing rim big off floor)
failed_approaches.why: The record shows no failure mechanism (auto_failure_mechanism: none), but the effects are small and noisy (rim share SE 0.295, PPP t=+1.1), so the outcome is inconclusive at N=1.07M possessions; the record cites small sample as the limitation.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on this play-by-play and reconstructed-lineup dataset (FAM:SF34) found a statistically detectable shift in play-type mix for a defensive-personnel condition, with some effects at |t|>2 (DRIVE, POST_UP, 3PA). This shows that shot-mix measures from this data have enough variance to show movement.
The same record found that rim share and PPP shifts were small and noisy, so shot-mix changes are detectable only for some outcomes and not reliably for efficiency.
Earlier project pipelines have produced leakage and construction artifacts (FAM:SF11, FAM:SF32), so any test built on this data needs leakage and label audits before its results can be trusted.
The only design-level placebo check recorded (FAM:SF-TMP-005) has no result, so no historical evidence establishes that a Design 5 placebo has been validated.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. FAM:SF34 concerns the opponent's rim big, and the other families concern kernel recommendations and openers.
No retrieved record reports an effect size, standard error or power for offensive-five substitutions specifically.
Whether the design can detect personnel effects is not established. FAM:SF-TMP-005, the only record naming a placebo, has no result.
The question's premise (that the design can detect personnel effects) is not shown by any retrieved result, so the question remains open.
Retrieval returned only the four family summaries; full records (read_family) were not opened, so any detail beyond the summaries is unverified.
own_inferences: The question as posed presupposes its answer. A positive shot-mix shift is the expected result, but the stated question does not specify a null or falsification, so a test needs to be built around the shift being absent under a placebo.

Offensive-five changes are not randomly assigned. Coaches substitute in response to score, fatigue, foul trouble and matchups, which are themselves related to shot selection. Any observed shot-mix change is therefore confounded unless these factors are conditioned on.

A shot-mix shift at the play-type level may be real but small (around 1pp, as in FAM:SF34), which implies that detecting it at useful power would need very large exposure within each team and lineup pair.

Splitting a single-season or single-team sample by lineup is likely to leave many lineup pairs with few possessions, which makes the EXPOSURE_SPARSITY risk material even when the total sample is around one million possessions.
uncertainties: The retrieved records do not state the number of offensive-five substitution events, lineup-pair exposures, or the minimum possessions per lineup in 2022-23 to 2024-25.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoff data was included in FAM:SF34 is not stated, so its sample may not match the planned sample.
Whether the Design 5 placebo in FAM:SF-TMP-005 corresponds to the offensive-five design in this question is unclear from the summary.
The retrieval results may not be complete; additional relevant records may exist that were not returned.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the retrieved evidence, the question would look like a straightforward within-team substitution analysis. The retrieved records changed the decision in three ways: (1) the closest precedent (FAM:SF34) found only small, inconclusive shot-mix effects in this dataset, which suggests the effect is small relative to noise; (2) earlier pipelines in this project produced leakage and construction artifacts (FAM:SF11, FAM:SF32), so an audit gate is required before any claim; (3) the one recorded placebo check (FAM:SF-TMP-005) has no result, so the design's ability to detect personnel effects is unvalidated. These findings moved the decision from an unconditional proceed to proceed_with_changes, with a placebo and power requirement set before analysis.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup-pair exposure within team and season may be too thin for the shot-mix comparisons needed; the minimum possessions per lineup must be set before analysis.
Prior work on this data (FAM:SF34) found only small, noisy shot-mix effects (rim SE 0.295; PPP t=+1.1), so detecting a plausible shift needs a pre-specified power calculation.
Offensive-five changes are endogenous to score state, fatigue, foul trouble and matchups; these must be conditioned on or the shot-mix change cannot be attributed to personnel.
The only retrieved placebo (FAM:SF-TMP-005) has no result, so the design's ability to produce a null under no personnel effect is unvalidated.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether offensive-five changes move shot mix. FAM:SF34 is the nearest work: it tested shot-mix response to an opponent-personnel condition on the same dataset and found small, mostly inconclusive effects. FAM:SF-TMP-005 names a Design 5 placebo but has no result. FAM:SF11 and FAM:SF32 are artifact-classified work on the same pipeline and show construction risks, not personnel effects.

risks.text: Lineup-pair exposure may be too sparse within team-seasons to estimate shot-mix changes reliably.
Effects of this size were recorded as small and noisy in FAM:SF34 (N=1.07M), so the design needs a power calculation before analysis.
Score state, fatigue, foul trouble and matchups drive substitutions and shot selection together, so changes in shot mix may reflect game context instead of personnel.
Lineups are chosen after bad stretches or favourable matchups, so lineup changes are selected on recent outcomes, which can bias shot-mix comparisons.
The Design 5 placebo has no recorded result (FAM:SF-TMP-005), so the design's null behaviour is unvalidated.
Earlier pipelines leaked future information (FAM:SF11), so shot-mix features computed from the full game could leak outcome information into lineup assignments.
Play-type and shot-mix labels are derived from play-by-play outcomes (points, shot result), so shot-mix classes may be partly defined by the outcomes they are meant to explain.
The defensive H2-adjustment trait was split-half tested in FAM:SF-TMP-005 with no result, so the reliability of play-type and shot-mix measures is unknown.
Several shot-mix outcomes (DRIVE, POST_UP, 3PA, rim, midrange) and several lineup contrasts would be tested together, inflating false positives without correction.
Shot mix and lineup usage change across 2022-23 to 2024-25, so pooling seasons may mix different rotation and pace regimes (noted in FAM:SF11 and FAM:SF32).
Lineup reconstruction from substitution intervals and starters may misassign players during substitutions, which would misattribute shots to the wrong offensive five.

methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detectably move shot mix in play-by-play data?
What confounders and reliability issues threaten a lineup-to-shot-mix design?
Is the design sufficiently powered given lineup exposure sparsity across 2022-23 to 2024-25?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
